newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev falls, eyes 1,000-per-mark peg plan.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev falls, eyes 1,000-per-mark peg plan.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 1,635-1,655 per dollar at the close from the morning's 1,580 after the Finance Minister announced plans to peg the lev at 1,000 per mark under a currency board system, dealers said.
"Mainly final clients were bidding for marks to profit on the pending pegging of the lev (at a fixed exchange rate) by the end of the month," a bank dealer said.
The mark was bid at 940-950 levs and offered at 970-980 levs at the close against 912/917 at the opening, tracking the dollar/mark on international markets.

"Exchange rates for the lev against major currencies other than the dollar are being calculated through the lev/dollar rate because the dollar has the largest share in (local forex trade) turnover," another dealer said.
Bulgaria's Finance Minister Muravei Radev said on Tuesday that the cabinet will propose to peg the lev at 1,000 per mark as an anchor in a currency board arrangement to be introduced on July 1.
Foreign currency demand from banks was relatively low as they have already built up forex positions in anticipation the lev would be pegged at 1,000 per mark or 1,600-1,700 per dollar.
Local banks also eyed weakening mark on international markets to convert some dollar positions into marks through arbitrage, traders said.
Local trade was expected to be calm in the next few days as resistance levels for the mark and the dollar were now close to the planned pegging rate.

"I do not expect much higher dollar or mark bids in the following days because there will be no substantial yields for the potential buyer if the lev is fixed at 1,000 per mark from next month," a third dealer said.

Even some profit taking might be seen at around 1,650-1,700 levs per dollar as investors could channel funds into lev-denominated government securities until the central bank main interest rate was still high enough, the trader added.
The main rate is now set at 48.72 percent annually. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
